questions.q:
The figure shows two solid discs with radius $R$ and~$r$~respectively. If mass per unit area is the same for both, what is the ratio of $MI$ of bigger disc around axis $AB$ (Which is $⊥$ to the plane of the disc and passing through its centre)$ of MI$ of smaller disc around one of its diameters lying on its plane? Given $M$ is the mass of the larger disc.

($MI$ stands for a moment of inertia)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Ratio of the moment of inertia $= \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2}MR^{2}}{\dfrac{1}{4}mr^{2}}$

$= \dfrac{2\sigma \piR^{2}R^{2}}{\sigma\pir^{2}r^{2}} = \dfrac{2R^{4}}{r4}$

questions.q:
A particle of mass $m$ is moving along a trajectory given by
$x = {x}_{0} + acos{\omega}_{1}t$
$y = {y}_{0} + bsin{\omega}_{2}t$
The torque, acting on the particle about the origin, at $t = 0$ is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$x = {x}_{0} + acos \left({\omega}_{1}t\right)$
$y = {y}_{0} + bsin \left({\omega}_{2}t\right)$
${a}_{x} = - a{\omega}_{1}^{2}\cos \left({\omega}_{1}$t\right)$
${a}_{y} = - b{\omega}_{2}^{2}\sin \left({\omega}_{2}t\right)$
At $t = 0$ ,
$\overset{→}{F} = m\overset{→}{a} = \lleft(-a{\omega}_{1}^{2}\overset{^}{i})$
And
$\overset{→}{r} = \left({x}_{0}\text{+}$a\right)\overset{^}{i} + {y}_{0}\overset{^}{j}$
Torque, $τ = \overset{→}{r} $\times \overset{→}{F}
$τ = \left( \left({x}_{0}\text{+}a\right)\overset{^}{i} + {y}_{0}\overset{^}{j}\right)\times \lleft(-a{\omega}_{1}^{2}\overset{^}{i})$
$= m{y}_{0}a{\omega}_{1}^{2}\overset{^}{k}$

questions.q: A spherical shell of $1$ kg mass and radius $R$ is rolling with angular speed $\omega$ on horizontal plane (as shown in figure). The magnitude of angular momentum of the shell about the origin $O$ is $\dfrac{a}{3}R^{2}\omega$. The value of $a$& will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Angular momentum of a rotating and translating body is given by,

${L}_{O} = mvR + I\omega = mvR + \dfrac{2}{3}MR^{2}\omega$

For rolling,~$v = \omegaR$

$⇒ {L}_{O} = m\omegaR^{2}\left(1 + \dfrac{2}{3}\right) = \dfrac{5}{3}m\omegaR^{2}$

Therefore, the value of~$a = 5$.

questions.q: Two uniform circular discs are rotating independently in the same direction around their common axis passing through their centres. The moment of inertia and angular velocity of the first disc are $0 . 1kg - m^{2}$~and~$10\text{rad}s^{- 1}$~respectively while those for the second one are $0 . 2kg - m^{2}$and~$5rads^{- 1}$& respectively. At some instant they get stuck together and start rotating as a single system about their common axis with some angular speed. The kinetic energy of the combined system is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Common angular velocity from angular momentum conversation

$\omega = \dfrac{{l}_{1}{ω}_{1} + {I}_{2}{ω}_{2}}{{I}_{1} + {I}_{2}} = \dfrac{0 . 1 \times 10 + 0 . 2 \times 5}{0 . 1 + 0 . 2} = \dfrac{20}{3}$
Final K.E.
${K}_{f} = \dfrac{1}{2}{I}_{1}{ω}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}{I}_{2}{ω}^{2}$
$= \dfrac{1}{2}\left(0 . 1 + 0 . 2\right) \times \left(\dfrac{20}{3}\right)2 ⇒ {k}_{f} = \dfrac{20}{3}$

Now the rod is cut into two equal parts and these parts are joined symmetrically to form a cross shape. Moment of inertia of cross about an axis passing through its center and normal to plane containing cross is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\alpha=\frac{\mathrm{M} \ell^2}{12}$
$\begin{aligned} & \alpha^{\prime}=2\left[\frac{\frac{\mathrm{M}}{2}\left(\frac{\ell}{2}\right)^2}{12}\right] \\ & \alpha^{\prime}=\frac{\mathrm{M} \ell^2}{48}=\frac{\alpha}{4}\end{aligned}$
Correct option is (2)

A rod of length $50$ cm is pivoted at one end. It is raised such that it makes an angle of ${30}^{o}$ from the horizontal as shown and released from rest. Its angular speed when it passes through the horizontal (in $rads^{- 1}$ ) will be \left(g = 10ms^{- 2}\right)$

$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From conservation of mechanical energy


Loss in gravitational $PE =$ gain in $KE$

$mg\dfrac{l}{2}sin {30}^{o} = \dfrac{1}{2}I{\omega}^{2}$

$mg\dfrac{l}{2}sin {30}^{o} = \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{ml^{2}}{3}{\omega}^{2}$

$\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{3g}{2l}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3 \times 10}{2 \times 50 \times {10}^{- 2}}} = \sqrt{30}rad / s$

questions.q:
A circular disk of radius R meter and mass M kg is rotating around the axis perpendicular to the disk. An external torque is applied to the disk such that $\theta(t)=5 t^2-8 t$, where $\theta(t)$ is the angular position of the rotating disc as a function of time $t$.
How much power is delivered by the applied torque, when $t=2 \mathrm{~s}$ ?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \theta=5 \mathrm{t}^2-8 \mathrm{t} \\
& \omega=\frac{\mathrm{d} \theta}{\mathrm{dt}}=10 \mathrm{t}-8 \\
& \alpha=\frac{\mathrm{d} \omega}{\mathrm{dt}}=10 \\
& \therefore \mathrm{p}=\tau \omega \\
& =(\mathrm{I} \alpha) \omega \\
& =\left(\frac{\mathrm{mR}^2}{2}\right) \alpha \omega \\
& =\left(\frac{\mathrm{mR}^2}{2}\right)(10)(10
\end{aligned}$ Put $\mathrm{t}=2\mathrm{p}=60 \mathrm{mR}^2$

questions.q: Moment of inertia of a cylinder of mass& $m,$~length $L$ and radius~$R$ about an axis passing through its centre and perpendicular to the axis of the cylinder is~$I = M\left(\dfrac{R2}{4} + \dfrac{L2}{12}\right) .$ If such a cylinder is to be made for a given mass of a material, the ratio~$\dfrac{L}{R}$ for it to have minimum possible $I$ is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let a cylinder of mass& ${m}_{1}$, length~$L$~and~radius~$R$~then~take elementary disc of radius~$R$~and trickiness~$dx$~at distance of~$x$~from axis~$OO '$~then moment of inertia about~$OO '$~as this element

$dl = \dfrac{dmR2}{4} + {dmx}^{2}$

$I = ∫ dl = ∫ \dfrac{dmR2}{4} + {∫}_{n = L / 2}^{n = - L / 2}\dfrac{M}{L}dx \times x^{2}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{MR2}{4} + \dfrac{ML2}{12}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{M}{4} \times \dfrac{V}{πL} + \dfrac{ML2}{12}$

$\dfrac{dI}{dL} = - \dfrac{mV}{4{πL}^{2}} + \dfrac{M \times 2L}{12} = 0$

$⇒ V = \dfrac{2}{3}{πL}^{3} ⇒ {πR}^{2}L = \dfrac{2}{3}{πL}^{3} ⇒ \dfrac{L}{R} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3}{2}} \left($I = \dfrac{MV}{4\pi L} + \dfrac{ML2}{12}\right)$

$

questions.q: A long cylindrical vessel is half filled with a liquid. When the vessel is rotated about its own vertical axis, the liquid rises up near the wall. If the radius of vessel is $5$ cm and its rotational speed is $2$ rotations per second, then the difference in the heights between the center and the sides, in $cm,$ will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
When cylinder is rotated, water will rise at the edge and will dip at the centre. The difference in pressure at $A$ and $O$ is ${P}_{A} - {P}_{0} = ρgh .$ Due to height difference.

pressure difference ${P}_{1} - {P}_{0} = ρ ⋅ {a}_{cm}R$ Due to rotation.

$= ρ ⋅ \left({\omega}^{2} . \dfrac{R}{2}\right)R$



$∴ ρgh = ρ\dfrac{{\omega}^{2}R^{2}}{2} ⇒ h = \dfrac{{\omega}^{2} ⋅ R^{2}}{2g} = {\left(2\pi \times 2\right)}^{2} \times \dfrac{{\left(0.05\right)}^{2}}{2 \times 10}$

$= 0.02m$

$= 2cm$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.

Assertion A: Moment of inertia of a circular disc of mass $M$~and radius $R$~about $X, Y$ axes (passing through its plane) and Z-axis which is perpendicular to its plane were found to be ${I}_{x}, {I}_{y}$ and ${I}_{z}$, respectively. The respective radii of gyration about all the three axes will be the same.

Reason R:& A rigid body making rotational motion has fixed mass and shape. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both A& and R& are correct but R& is not the correct explanation of A.
A& is not correct but R& is correct.
A is correct but R& is not correct.

Both A& and R& are correct and R& is the correct
explanation of A.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
${I}_{z} = {I}_{x} + {I}_{y}$ (using perpendicular axis theorem)

and~$I = mk^{2} ( K:$ radius of gyration)~

so $m{K}_z^{2} = m{K}_x^{2} + m{K}_y^{2}$

${K}_z^{2} = {K}_x^{2} + {K}_y^{2}$

So radius of gyration about axes $x, y$~and~$z$ will not be same, hence assertion& A& is not correct reason R is correct statement (property of a rigid body).

questions.q: A force of $- P\overset{^}{k}$~acts on the origin of the coordinate system. The torque about the point $( 2, - 3 )$ is $P ( a\overset{^}{i} + b\overset{^}{j} )$, The ratio of $\dfrac{a}{b}$ is $\dfrac{x}{2}$. The value of $x$ is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
It is given that the force& $\overset{→}{F} = - P\overset{^}{k}$

The coordinates of the origin is~$( 0, 0 )$.

The coordinates of the point given is $( 2, - 3 )$

The displacement vector is~

$\overset{→}{r} = ( 0 - 2 ) \overset{^}{i} + ( 0 + 3 ) \overset{^}{j} = - 2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j}$

Hence, the torque is~

$\overset{→}{τ} = \overset{→}{r} \times \overset{→}{F} = ( - 2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} ) \times ( - P\overset{^}{k} )$

$⇒ \overset{→}{τ} = - 2P\overset{^}{j} - 3P\overset{^}{i} = P ( a\overset{^}{i} + b\overset{^}{j} )$

So, it can be written

$a = - 3$,~$b = - 2$

$∴ \dfrac{a}{b} = \left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right) ⇒$ so $x = 3$

The position vectors of two 1 kg particles, (A) and (B), are given by
$\overrightarrow{\mathrm{r}}_{\mathrm{A}}=\left(\alpha_1 \mathrm{t}^2 \hat{i}+\alpha_2 \mathrm{t} \hat{j}+\alpha_3 \mathrm{t} \hat{k}\right) \mathrm{m}$ and $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{r}}_{\mathrm{B}}=\left(\beta_1 \mathrm{t} \hat{i}+\beta_2 \mathrm{t}^2 \hat{j}+\beta_3 \mathrm{t} \hat{k}\right) \mathrm{m}$, respectively; \left(\alpha_1=1 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2, \alpha_2=3 \mathrm{n} \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}, \alpha_3=2 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}, \beta_1=2 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}, \beta_2=-1 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2, \beta_3=4 \mathrm{pm} / \mathrm{s}\right)$, where t is time, n and p are constants. At $t=1 \mathrm{~s},\left|\overrightarrow{V_A}\right|=\left|\vec{V}_B\right|$ and velocities $\vec{V}_A$ and $\vec{V}_B$ of the particles are orthogonal to each other. At $t=1 \mathrm{~s}$, the magnitude of angular momentum of particle (A) with respect to the position of particle (B) is $\sqrt{\mathrm{L}} \mathrm{kgm}^2 \mathrm{~s}^{-1}$. The value of L is _______ .$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
At $t=1r_{A B}=-1 \hat{i}+(3 n+1) \hat{j}+(2-4 p) \hat{k}$ At $t=1$\begin{aligned}
& v_A=2 \hat{i}+3 n \hat{j}+2 \hat{k} \\
& v_B=2 \hat{i}-2 \hat{j}+4 p \hat{k} \\
& \vec{v}_A-\vec{v}_B=0, \quad 4-6 n+8 p=0
\end{aligned}$\begin{gathered}\left|v_A\right|=\left|v_B\right| \quad(3 n)^2+4=4+16 p^2 \\ 3 n=-4 p \\ 4+16 p=0 \\ p=-\frac{1}{4}, n=\frac{1}{3} \\ r_{A B}=-\hat{i}+2 \hat{j}+3 \hat{k} \\ v_A=2 \hat{i}+\hat{j}+2 \hat{k} \\ \therefore L=m\left|\vec{r}_{A B} \times \vec{v}_A\right|=90\end{gathered}$
